text: I closed out the quarter reviewing the forecast account by account with each rep; when I saw TechCorreio was going to slip to July, I rebuilt the week's plan in one afternoon and redistributed the hot accounts. I'd rather rework the plan ten times than accept ending the month below target.

text: This week I finally migrated my one-on-ones to the new calendar and took the chance to update the proposal templates in the team drive. I also switched the Monday meeting room because the old one had no TV to project the pipeline.

text: I promised Ricardo I'd send the Brastel proposal on Tuesday and let it slip. Wednesday morning he was at my desk asking what had happened and what I needed so it wouldn't happen again. He writes down every commitment from the pipeline review and follows up on each one the following week.

text: When the June number got tight, Ricardo cancelled his own trip to the event in São Paulo to stay on top of the renewals. He keeps repeating that an effort trophy doesn't pay the quota, and he holds the team's results and his own to the same hard standard.

text: I've set aside my Wednesday mornings to train Camila and Mateus on discovery calls: we record the calls, listen together, and I show them where a question could have opened the client up more. text: Last week I cleaned up my CRM and archived about forty old opportunities that still showed up on my dashboard. I also took the chance to update the contacts on the Ardosia account, who had changed emails after the merger.

I lost a big lead because I skipped the qualification step and went to tell Helena expecting a scolding. She thanked me for flagging it quickly, said that a mistake reported early is a cheap mistake, and built a checklist with me for the next calls. It was the first time since I joined that making a mistake didn't feel like the end of the world.

text: My onboarding here was basically Helena: she put together a thirty-day plan, sat next to me on my first cold calls and then gave me line-by-line feedback on what I'd said. While the rest of the team chased their own quotas, she set aside an hour a day for me.

tags.quote: sat next to me on my first cold calls and then gave me line-by-line feedback

text: Before sending the Coplan proposal I asked Helena to review it; she restructured the pricing page with me and taught me the rationale she uses to anchor the discount, instead of simply correcting it. She's the only person on the team who pauses her own prospecting to develop others.

text: After a tense quarter in sales, Helena reached out to me and we designed a team retro together; she prepared the agenda, made sure the SDRs spoke before the seniors and closed with clear agreements on who does what.
